deck_context.source_summary: Class 18 follows the Sling Models and Model Exporter lesson. It teaches when reusable work belongs in an OSGi service, how Declarative Services owns lifecycle and dependencies, how typed configuration becomes effective in AEM as a Cloud Service, and why a new servlet is justified only by a distinct HTTP consumer and contract.
deck_context.core_claim: Add only the boundary the consumer needs: one reusable service capability, one safe effective configuration and no new servlet unless an existing rendering or export surface cannot satisfy a real HTTP contract.
canonical_facts: A service should own one reusable capability needed by at least one real consumer.
Declarative Services registers components, manages their lifecycle and resolves declared service references.
A required unsatisfied service reference prevents component activation.
OSGi Metatype annotations describe typed operator-facing configuration metadata.
@Designate connects a Declarative Services component PID to an Object Class Definition.
AEM as a Cloud Service supports author or publish plus dev, stage or prod run modes; custom run modes are not supported.
For one PID, the configuration with the most matching run modes is effective as a whole; properties are not merged from less-specific files.
$[env:NAME] represents a non-secret environment-specific value and $[secret:NAME] represents a secret value.
Environment variables must not override Adobe-owned OSGi configuration.
Local runtime state is inspected in the SDK Web Console; cloud state is inspected in Developer Console status dumps.
HTL, a Sling Model, a Core Component or an existing Model Exporter contract should be preferred before a new servlet.
Sling strongly recommends resource-type servlet registration over path binding.
A servlet registration should constrain methods, selectors and extensions to the real contract.
A new endpoint adds validation, authorization, caching and compatibility responsibilities.

slides.title: Create a service only for a reusable capability.
slides.intent: Prevent speculative service layers while giving shared or external work one explicit owner.
key_points: Start with a real consumer and one named capability.
Use a service for reusable queries, integrations or orchestration.
Keep presentation logic in the Sling Model.
Do not create a pass-through service.

slides.title: Declarative Services owns the runtime lifecycle.
slides.intent: Show how a service becomes available and why consumers depend on its registered capability.
key_points: @Component registers GuideUrlService.
DS creates, activates and deactivates the component.
@Reference declares a real dependency.
Unsatisfied required references block activation.

local_context.required_background: Use a five-stage runtime chain: IMPLEMENTATION CLASS → BUNDLE METADATA → DS COMPONENT → SERVICE REGISTRY → CONSUMERS. Show @Component(service = GuideUrlService.class) at registration. Add one required @Reference entering the DS component through a gate labeled SATISFIED? YES → ACTIVE; NO → UNSATISFIED. Do not show manual new construction.

layout.composition: Horizontal lifecycle and registration pipeline with a vertical required-reference gate before activation.
layout.intent: Connect Java annotations to observable runtime component and service state.

visual_elements.main_visual: Declarative Services lifecycle pipeline and required-reference activation gate.

constraints: Spell @Component, GuideUrlService.class and @Reference exactly.
Do not imply the implementation registers itself through construction.
Keep ACTIVE and UNSATISFIED as distinct runtime states.

slides.title: Typed configuration documents an operational contract.
slides.intent: Connect Metatype definitions to readable typed service configuration.
key_points: @ObjectClassDefinition names the contract.
Methods declare property names, types and defaults.
@AttributeDefinition adds operator guidance.
@Designate connects the component PID.

local_context.required_background: Place GUIDE URL CONFIG in the center with exact annotations @ObjectClassDefinition and @AttributeDefinition. Show two typed methods: String base_url() and boolean enabled() default true. Flow to GENERATED METATYPE METADATA, then @Designate(ocd = GuideUrlConfig.class), then the service PID, then ACTIVATE WITH TYPED CONFIG. Add OPERATIONAL API as the conclusion.

layout.composition: Annotated configuration-interface cutaway flowing through generated metadata and PID into typed activation.
layout.intent: Make configuration shape, documentation and runtime consumption one connected contract.

visual_elements.main_visual: Metatype interface → metadata → Designate/PID → typed activation flow.

constraints: Spell all annotations and GuideUrlConfig.class exactly.
Render String and boolean types clearly.
Do not show loose string parsing as the recommended path.

slides.title: Effective configuration is selected per PID.
slides.intent: Explain AEM as a Cloud Service configuration selection without Java environment conditionals.
key_points: Supported run modes select one complete PID configuration.
The most matching run modes wins.
More specific replaces; it does not merge.
Custom run modes are unsupported.

slides.title: Values vary by environment; secrets stay out of Git.
slides.intent: Separate versioned configuration shape from deploy-time values and credentials.
key_points: Commit stable configuration and placeholder names.
Use $[env:GUIDE_BASE_URL] for non-secret values.
Use $[secret:GUIDE_API_TOKEN] for secrets.
Never commit, log or capture resolved secrets.

local_context.required_background: Use three vertical zones. VERSIONED IN GIT contains the stable PID JSON and placeholder names only. DEPLOY-TIME VALUES splits into ENV with $[env:GUIDE_BASE_URL] and SECRET with $[secret:GUIDE_API_TOKEN]. EFFECTIVE SERVICE receives resolved baseUrl and a masked token. Add a redaction shield and warning: DO NOT OVERRIDE ADOBE-OWNED OSGi CONFIGURATION.

layout.composition: Three-zone configuration supply chain with separate environment and secret channels.
layout.intent: Make the storage and exposure boundary for each value class unmistakable.

visual_elements.main_visual: Versioned configuration shape receiving distinct ENV and SECRET deploy-time inputs.

constraints: Render both placeholder expressions exactly.
Mask the effective token; never invent a credential value.
Do not place resolved secrets in Git, logs or screenshots.

slides.title: Missing configuration must fail safely and visibly.
slides.intent: Avoid insecure fallbacks and silent partial behavior when required configuration is absent or invalid.
key_points: Classify required, optional and capability-enabling properties.
Validate values at activation.
Reject unsafe configuration.
Otherwise disable with a useful diagnostic.

local_context.required_background: Start with CONFIGURATION INPUTS: base URL, enabled flag and token-present signal; do not show a token. Send them through VALIDATE AT ACTIVATION with three checks: HTTPS URL, ALLOWED RANGE / VALUE, REQUIRED SECRET PRESENT. Outcomes: VALID → ACTIVE in green; OPTIONAL ABSENCE → DISABLED WITH DIAGNOSTIC in navy; UNSAFE INPUT → ACTIVATION REJECTED in orange. Add NO SILENT PARTIAL BEHAVIOR.

layout.composition: Central validation gate with three input checks and three deliberately separated runtime outcomes.
layout.intent: Teach safe failure as an explicit lifecycle decision.

constraints: Do not display a secret value.
Keep ACTIVE, DISABLED WITH DIAGNOSTIC and ACTIVATION REJECTED distinct.
Do not recommend an insecure fallback URL or token.

slides.title: Verify the effective runtime value, not only the file.
slides.intent: Teach developers to prove which configuration and component state the runtime actually applied.
key_points: Use the SDK Web Console locally.
Use Developer Console status dumps in cloud environments.
Match PID, tier, component state and non-secret values.
Verify Author and Publish independently.

AEM AS A CLOUD SERVICE → DEVELOPER CONSOLE → Components + Configurations status dumps. Both converge on an evidence checklist with exact rows: PID, TIER / POD, COMPONENT STATE, NON-SECRET EFFECTIVE VALUES. Add AUTHOR ≠ PUBLISH when configured differently and REDACT SECRETS.

layout.composition: Mirrored local and cloud diagnostic lanes converging on one runtime evidence checklist.
layout.intent: Shift proof from source files to observable effective state.

visual_elements.main_visual: Web Console and Developer Console evidence paths.

constraints: Use Web Console only for local SDK and Developer Console for cloud evidence.

slides.title: Choose the minimum delivery surface for the consumer.
slides.intent: Make no new servlet the default unless a requirement needs a separate HTTP contract.
key_points: HTL for server-rendered component markup.
Sling Model for prepared values and state.
Reuse an existing Core Component or Model Exporter contract.
Servlet only for a distinct HTTP consumer and response contract.

local_context.required_background: Use a descending stop-at-first-fit ladder beginning with WHAT DOES THE CONSUMER NEED? Rung 1 HTL — SERVER-RENDERED MARKUP. Rung 2 SLING MODEL — PREPARED VALUES / STATE. Rung 3 EXISTING CORE COMPONENT OR MODEL EXPORTER — EXISTING CONTRACT. Rung 4 NEW SERVLET — DISTINCT HTTP CONSUMER + RESPONSE CONTRACT. Place validation, authorization, caching and compatibility weights on the servlet rung. Conclude THE BEST SERVLET MAY BE NO SERVLET.

layout.composition: Four-rung decision ladder with a visible stop marker on each existing surface and accumulated responsibility on the servlet rung.
layout.intent: Encode the minimum-surface rule as a practical design sequence.

visual_elements.main_visual: HTL → Sling Model → existing contract → servlet decision ladder.

constraints: Render all four surfaces and their consumer need exactly.
Keep the servlet as the final conditional rung.

slides.title: If a servlet is required, bind and constrain it explicitly.
slides.intent: Define the smallest safe servlet registration and the evidence needed to operate it.
key_points: Prefer resource-type registration over path binding.
Declare exact methods, selectors and extensions.
Validate inputs and return deliberate responses.
Verify permissions, cache behavior and servlet resolution.
